result.conclusion: No. The current intake collects many relevant signals (VA contact, ADLs, basic income range, caregiver coresidence and relationship) but does NOT gather all facts needed for a defensible preliminary eligibility conclusion for the VA pathways you actually screen for (PCAFC and VA Pension including Aid & Attendance/Housebound). It is only sufficient for triage. Below are focused screening gaps (<=12) that must be closed to reach a defensible preliminary conclusion, followed by application-only actions, visibility gaps, unsupported/stale claims, and scope limits.

screening_gaps.criterion: Minimum active-duty/wartime service and character of discharge
screening_gaps.pathway: VA Pension (and Aid & Attendance eligibility presupposes pension eligibility)
missing_facts: Exact active-duty entry and separation dates
Whether service included at least one day during a recognized wartime period (dates/locations)
Character of discharge (was it under conditions other than dishonorable?)
screening_gaps.trigger: User indicates 'Veteran' (recipient.military_status) or selects Pension/Aid & Attendance as a goal
simple_questions: What were the veteran’s active-duty start and end dates (MM/YYYY)?
Do you have the veteran’s DD214 or other discharge paperwork? If not, was the discharge 'other than dishonorable'?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If veteran appears income/asset-eligible for pension or requests A&A screening, request DD214 or VA service record to verify service/wartime and discharge facts before concluding eligibility.
screening_gaps.caveat: The Federal Benefits Guide describes service and discharge requirements but does not give the granular exceptions; verify with VA records or DD214.

screening_gaps.criterion: VA health-care enrollment status and VA facility/PACT (VA enrollment distinct from any VA contact)
screening_gaps.pathway: PCAFC and other VA caregiver supports (PGCSS/PCAFC)
missing_facts: Whether the veteran is actively enrolled in VA health care (not just prior contact)
VA facility/PACT managing care or VA patient identifier (VHIC/VA file number)
screening_gaps.trigger: Case.goals includes 'Finding VA caregiver benefits' OR recipient.va_contact = 'Yes'/'I'm not sure'
simple_questions: Is the veteran currently enrolled in VA health care (Yes/No)?
If Yes: what VA facility or PACT manages their care (name/city) and do they have a VHIC or VA patient ID?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If the user wants PCAFC or enhanced VA caregiver services, read caregiver.va.gov or pull VA enrollment records to confirm enrollment and PACT before claiming eligibility.
screening_gaps.caveat: VA contact in intake can mean many things; PCAFC eligibility requires enrollment and specific VA case management—caregiver.va.gov must be consulted (not present in the retrieved pages).

screening_gaps.criterion: PCAFC primary family caregiver designation, coresidence and actual caregiving hours
screening_gaps.pathway: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC)
missing_facts: Whether caregiver is or will be designated the veteran’s Primary Family Caregiver under PCAFC
Typical hours of hands-on personal care provided (hours/day or hrs/week)
Detailed co-residence timing (whether they live together continuously when PCAFC requires it)
screening_gaps.trigger: User selects 'Finding VA caregiver benefits' or indicates VA contact/enrollment
simple_questions: Are you the veteran’s primary family caregiver who provides most of their personal care (Yes/No)?
About how many hours per day or per week do you provide hands-on care?
Do you currently live with the veteran full-time, part-time, or not at all?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: Before recommending PCAFC as likely — consult caregiver.va.gov eligibility criteria and VA case manager guidance to confirm caregiver-role/coresidence rules.
screening_gaps.caveat: The Federal Benefits Guide points to caregiver.va.gov for PCAFC rules; the intake must capture primary-caregiver facts that the guide enforces but does not enumerate here.

screening_gaps.criterion: VA disability/service-connection rating details required to evaluate PCAFC/related supports
screening_gaps.pathway: PCAFC and other VA benefits that consider disability rating
missing_facts: Exact combined VA disability rating percentage and service-connection details
Date of rating decision and copy of decision letter
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.va_rating_assigned = 'Yes' or case.goals includes VA caregiver benefits
simple_questions: Has VA assigned a combined disability percentage? If so, what is the combined percent (e.g., 70%)?
Do you have the VA decision letter or rating notice?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: When caregiver/PCAFC screening is positive or near threshold — obtain VA decision letter to confirm rating and its effective date.
screening_gaps.caveat: PCAFC eligibility rules depend on specific service-connected conditions and ratings; the Federal Guide does not provide PCAFC’s full rating criteria — consult caregiver.va.gov or the PCAFC spec.

screening_gaps.criterion: Precise gross annual household income and countable net worth (not just monthly ranges)
screening_gaps.pathway: VA Pension (means-tested eligibility and A&A countable income calculations)
missing_facts: Total gross annual household income (all sources) for the veteran and spouse
Approximate total countable assets/net worth (specifying exclusions such as primary residence if applicable)
Unreimbursed medical expenses total for the relevant year (to reduce countable income)
screening_gaps.trigger: User selects Pension/Aid & Attendance or monthly income range suggests low income
simple_questions: What is the household’s gross annual income (all sources) for the last 12 months?
Approximately what is the veteran’s total countable assets/net worth (exclude primary residence if known)?
List unreimbursed medical/LTC expenses in the past 12 months and annual total.
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: Before a defensible pension eligibility conclusion; financial documents or agency calculations are required for accuracy.
screening_gaps.caveat: Monthly income ranges in intake are adequate for triage but insufficient for a defensible preliminary means-test determination.

screening_gaps.criterion: Medical evidence and clinician willingness to complete VA Form 21-2680 (Aid & Attendance / Housebound)
screening_gaps.pathway: VA Pension — Aid & Attendance or Housebound allowance
missing_facts: Whether an attending physician will complete VA Form 21-2680 and provide a detailed medical report describing ADL limitations
Specific ADL-level evidence linked to A&A definitions (which ADLs and how often assistance is required)
screening_gaps.trigger: ADL dependence reported or applicant expresses interest in Aid & Attendance
simple_questions: Is there an attending physician willing to complete VA Form 21-2680 (Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance)?
Which ADLs does the veteran need help with and how frequently?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If user intends to pursue A&A, request VA Form 21-2680 and physician/nursing reports before concluding eligibility.
screening_gaps.caveat: Self-report of ADLs is usable for triage only; the Form 21-2680 and clinician report are mandatory at application to establish A&A.

screening_gaps.criterion: Household composition, tax dependency and which incomes are countable
screening_gaps.pathway: Means-tested programs: VA Pension income calculations, SSI/SSDI/Medicaid interactions
missing_facts: A roster of household members with ages and relationships (to compute household unit)
Who claims whom on taxes (tax dependency and filing status)
Which income streams belong to the veteran vs spouse/other household members
screening_gaps.trigger: Any means-test pathway or tax-credit/tax-benefit goal selected
simple_questions: List everyone living in the household (name or initials), age, relationship to veteran, and whether they are claimed as a tax dependent.
Which incomes (Social Security, pensions, wages) are the veteran’s vs spouse’s?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: When income or asset totals are near eligibility thresholds; tax returns or benefit letters may be required for verification.
screening_gaps.caveat: Household composition materially changes countable income/net worth and the eligibility unit; intake must collect these to reach defensible conclusions.

screening_gaps.criterion: State and immigration/residency facts needed for Medicaid/Medi-Cal pathways (do not assume citizenship excludes CA Medi‑Cal)
screening_gaps.pathway: Medicaid / Medi‑Cal and programs that coordinate with VA (state-level eligibility)
missing_facts: State of residence (if intake is national), duration of residency in state, and specific state program name (Medi‑Cal in CA)
Immigration/citizenship or lawful presence status relevant to state Medicaid eligibility
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.medicaid_status is not 'Enrolled now' or user asks about Medicaid/Medi‑Cal eligibility
simple_questions: What state does the veteran live in (state name)?
Are they a U.S. citizen or do they have lawful immigrant status (Yes/No/Prefer not to say)?
How long have they lived continuously in this state?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If user wants Medi‑Cal guidance or state Medicaid long‑term care screening, consult state-specific Medi‑Cal rules and current state policy pages.
screening_gaps.caveat: Do NOT assume citizenship uniformly excludes California Medi‑Cal pathways; state rules can carve out pathways for certain non‑citizen categories — check state sources.

screening_gaps.criterion: Asset transfer timing and amounts relevant to state Medicaid (lookback) and other programs
screening_gaps.pathway: State Medicaid / long‑term‑care eligibility (Medi‑Cal), and any pathway where past transfers change countable assets
missing_facts: Whether transfers/gifts occurred and exact dates and amounts during the relevant state/program lookback period (often 30 months for some Medicaid LTC programs but varies by state and time)
Recipient of transfers and legal documentation
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.living_setting = 'Nursing home or skilled nursing facility' OR user interested in Medicaid long‑term care
simple_questions: Has the veteran transferred or given away money/property in the last 30 months? If Yes: list dates, amounts, and recipients.
Have any transfers been for fair value (sale) vs gift?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: Before concluding Medicaid/Medi‑Cal LTC eligibility; check state policy for lookback period and penalty calculations.
screening_gaps.caveat: Asset transfer rules are date-sensitive and state-specific; the Federal Benefits Guide is not exhaustive for state Medicaid transfer rules.

screening_gaps.criterion: Expected continuous, long-term need for personal care (timeline / prognosis) required by PCAFC and A&A screening
screening_gaps.pathway: PCAFC; VA Aid & Attendance (the VA six‑month/continuous care requirement)
missing_facts: Clinical prognosis or expected duration of continuous in-person care and whether need is expected to continue at least 6 months
Specific pattern (continuous daily in-person personal care vs intermittent supervision)
screening_gaps.trigger: Case.goals includes PCAFC or A&A or recipient.va_six_month_care_need = 'I'm not sure'
simple_questions: Is the need for continuous in‑person personal care expected to last at least 6 months? (Yes/No/I'm not sure) If Yes: approximate expected end date or prognosis.
Is the care primarily hands‑on (bathing, dressing, transfers) or supervision for safety?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: When screening positive for PCAFC or A&A; request clinician prognosis or care-plan notes for a defensible conclusion.
screening_gaps.caveat: Intake question exists but is binary; you need more detail and clinical corroboration to rely on it.

application_only: Obtain VA Form 21-2680 completed by an attending physician (Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance) — see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:82:a1847a637a and VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:47:e3f77b29f7.

Obtain VA Form 21P-527EZ (Application for Veterans Pension) and supporting financial documentation (bank statements, benefit award letters, tax returns) — see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:46:d8c7218979 and VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:4:5d73ea8968.
Request DD214 or equivalent service/medical discharge documentation to verify service dates and character of discharge (application stage for pension) — see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:45:9ec6aec9ad.

Obtain VA rating decision letters or award notices to confirm combined disability percentage and service‑connection details (application/supporting evidence for PCAFC) — see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:33:b75e51512c.
Gather detailed financial schedules and an asset inventory (dates and values) including any transfers for Medicaid/Medi‑Cal long‑term care determinations (state forms and lookback documentation).

Collect clinician narratives or facility reports describing ADL dependence and prognosis (physician or nursing home reports) to support A&A or PCAFC claims — see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:82:a1847a637a.

If pursuing PCAFC, obtain VA caregiver-designation paperwork and coordinate with VA case manager/PACT to confirm enrollment routes via caregiver.va.gov (Federal Benefits Guide points to that site: VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:33:b75e51512c).
visibility_gaps: Household roster with ages and relationships (needed to compute eligibility unit and countable income): intake asks household size but not member ages/relationships.
Tax dependency and who claims whom on tax returns (affects dependent status and income unit): intake asks support and living together questions but not tax-filing relationships.
Clear ownership and attribution of income streams (which income is veteran’s vs spouse’s vs other household members): intake uses household income ranges only.
Precise VA enrollment details (facility/PACT and patient ID) — intake records VA contact but not enrollment or PACT assignment.
Caregiver primary‑designation and exact caregiving hours — intake asks relationship and some coresidence but not formal designation or hours quantified.
unsupported_or_stale_claims: Implying that any 'VA contact' equals VA health‑care enrollment and therefore PCAFC eligibility — intake equates contact with potential PCAFC pathway without confirming enrollment. (See VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:33:b75e51512c and :33:abe7dd19a9 which point to caregiver.va.gov for PCAFC criteria.)

Using a coarse monthly income range as sufficient to determine VA Pension eligibility — VA pension requires annual income/net‑worth review and unreimbursed medical expenses to compute countable income (see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:46:d8c7218979).

Assuming asset/transfer rules are uniform and that a 30‑month transfer question is definitive — asset lookback and transfer penalty rules are state‑sensitive (for Medicaid/Medi‑Cal) and date‑sensitive; the Federal Guide does not define state lookbacks (see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:4:5d73ea8968).
Treating 'recipient.va_six_month_care_need' checkbox as equivalent to clinical documentation — the Guide requires physician reports/VA Form 21-2680 for A&A (VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:82:a1847a637a).
scope_limits: This audit evaluates only whether the intake collects the facts needed for a defensible preliminary screening conclusion (triage). It does NOT determine final eligibility, make application decisions, or advise on appeals or legal strategy.

PCAFC and some VA decisions depend on VA clinical review and case‑management determinations (caregiver.va.gov and VA case managers); the Federal Benefits Guide references caregiver.va.gov but does not contain PCAFC’s full adjudicative criteria — you must consult caregiver.va.gov or VA policy for final rules (see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:33:b75e51512c).

State Medicaid/Medi‑Cal rules (lookback periods, transfer penalty treatment, non‑citizen eligibility) are state and date sensitive; the Federal Benefits Guide provides links but not exhaustive state policy—state sources must be consulted for Medicaid decisions (see VA-FEDERAL-BENEFITS-GUIDE:4:2deb359a49 and :4:5d73ea8968).

The intake purposely avoids requesting sensitive identifiers (SSNs, BICs, account numbers) — that limits automatic verification and means more document collection at the application stage will be required.
